ip_top_stories.title: Suno Loses Copyright Lawsuit To GEMA—AI Music Companies Should Worry
ip_top_stories.summary: German performing rights society GEMA has won a significant copyright case against AI music generator Suno, with the court ruling that AI models built on unlicensed intellectual property have no legal protection. The decision is being seen as a landmark ruling with broad implications for AI music companies. Following the verdict, Suno has also announced it will add watermarking to its outputs.

ip_top_stories.title: Meta Seeks To Block Zuckerberg Depo In AI Copyright Cases
ip_top_stories.summary: Meta is seeking to block the deposition of Mark Zuckerberg in ongoing AI copyright litigation. The move signals the high stakes of the cases for the company as plaintiffs push to question its chief executive directly about decisions related to AI training data.

ip_top_stories.title: Anthropic Pushes to Dismiss Copyright Lawsuit Over AI Training
ip_top_stories.summary: Anthropic has filed to dismiss a copyright lawsuit brought against it over the use of copyrighted material in AI training. The case is part of a broader wave of litigation testing the boundaries of fair use and AI training data practices in US courts.

ip_top_stories.title: The great book grab: Who gets to own knowledge in the age of AI?
ip_top_stories.summary: A broad examination of how AI companies are ingesting books and other published works to train their models, raising fundamental questions about ownership of knowledge and the rights of authors and publishers. The piece explores the tension between AI development and intellectual property protections in the publishing sector.

ip_top_stories.title: Delhi HC ruling on ANI-OpenAI copyright case sparks debate over fair dealing and judicial activism
ip_top_stories.summary: India's Delhi High Court has issued a ruling in the copyright case brought by news agency ANI against OpenAI, prompting significant debate among legal commentators over the court's interpretation of fair dealing provisions and the limits of judicial intervention in AI policy. The case has implications for how AI companies operating in India handle news content for training purposes.

ip_further_links.title: Not So Free to Roam: Australia's Shifting Approach to Copyright Protection in the Age of AI
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis of how Australia is reassessing its copyright framework in response to AI, signalling a tightening of protections that could affect how AI developers access and use Australian-published content.

ip_further_links.title: No news content for AI-training without licences | Hindustan Times
ip_further_links.summary: A report on growing calls and emerging regulatory moves to require AI companies to obtain licences before using news content for training, reflecting pressure from publishers worldwide.

ip_further_links.title: The AI Content Wars: Copyright, Fair Use, Training Data and the Future of Human Creation
ip_further_links.summary: A broad overview of the ongoing legal and ethical battles over AI training data, covering fair use doctrine, copyright claims, and what the outcomes could mean for human creators.

ip_further_links.title: Suno Adds Watermarking as It Loses the GEMA Copyright Case
ip_further_links.summary: Following its defeat in the GEMA copyright case, Suno has announced it will introduce watermarking technology to its AI-generated music outputs.

ip_further_links.title: Why AI companies are cutting up books to train AI models
ip_further_links.summary: An examination of the practice of using book content as AI training data, exploring the technical and legal dimensions of how publishers' and authors' works are being processed by AI developers.

ip_further_links.title: Suno muscles into vinyl market, plans to let users press their AI songs onto 12-inch records
ip_further_links.summary: Suno is expanding its commercial offering by allowing users to press AI-generated songs onto vinyl records, a move that raises further questions about the commercial exploitation of AI-created music amid its ongoing copyright disputes.

ip_further_links.title: Vietnam eyes new rules for AI, cross-border book platforms
ip_further_links.summary: Vietnam is considering new regulatory frameworks to govern AI use and cross-border digital book platforms, reflecting a widening international effort to address AI and publishing policy.
